Question: In ancient times, was it possible to treat fabrics or clothes to make them waterproof to some degree?
Answer: It is not clear what period is being called out as “ancient” in this question - but before the industrial revolution and the progress in water-proofing methods as per modern science, fabrics were treated to make them water-resistant. (Please keep in mind that water-proof even today a big call - most raincoats are certified as water-repellent or water-resitant). The traditional method was to apply linseed oil or dunk the fabric in wax. The common method was to mix the linseed oil in turpentine and then soak the fabric in it. (Turpentine at the time was distilled from the resin of pine trees). Once the fabric was soaked in the mixture, it was allowed to dry - when the turpentine would evaporate, leaving behind fabric impregnated with oil or wax. This was called oil skin and used on ships and in marine environments.
